messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated artifact fetch failures observed for Hugging Face hosted assets (429s + intermittent 403s). Affects new cold-starts in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Paging: @eli-nguyen

eli-nguyen: seeing a spike in cold-start timeouts. Fetcher is failing to download model shards for rdw-models/llama-3-7b. Rough numbers: ~28% cold-start fail rate for instances that need a fetch, latency tail doubled.

maria-khan: verified in fetch logs: repeated 429 with x-rate-limit headers present. Sometimes returns 403 shortly after. Example snippet:

```
2026-03-14T08:54:12Z fetcher[pid=4412] WARN hf_fetch failed code=429 url=https://huggingface.co/rdw-models/llama-3-7b/shard-5.bin headers={"x-rate-limit-remaining":"0","x-rate-limit-reset":"15"}
```

infra-sre: looks like we tripped a rate cap at HF. Prefetcher had a burst during a canary and multiple hosts share egress, so the effective concurrency to HF increased. Also seeing some S3 mirror 404s which prevents fallback for a subset of shards.

eli-nguyen: customer impact: a few enterprise tenants reported degraded throughput; default behavior is to attempt fetch -> timeout -> runtime 503. No PII exposure. Low-severity for in-flight requests but high disruption for new cold-starts.

maria-khan: tried standard backoff (exp backoff + jitter) but HF still returns 429 after 2-3 retries for same shard. Their headers indicate short windows. Suspect they throttle anonymous pulls more aggressively.

eli-nguyen: live mitigation proposal:
- Promote hot models to our S3 mirrors for affected regions (emergency mirroring).
- Reduce prefetch concurrency per-region and add per-host rate limit to avoid bursty behavior.
- Allow runtime fallback to quantized smaller variant for non-critical tiers (free/dev) while preserving premium paths.
- Open support ticket with HF requesting throttle details and/or auth-based higher limits.

oncall-pager: @eli-nguyen taking lead for the next hour. Start mirror promotion and apply prefetch limits now.

maria-khan: promote command (run on runbook box):

```
mirrorctl promote --model rdw-models/llama-3-7b --regions eu-west-1,us-west-2 --dest s3://rdw-emergency-mirrors/ --job emergency-20260314
```

infra-sre: apply temporary prefetch patch via API gateway config:

```
PATCH /api/config/prefetch
{
  "max_concurrent_fetches": 4,
  "per_host_limit": 8
}
```

eli-nguyen: patch applied in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Observability shows active HF connections drop ~65% within 45s.

maria-khan: promotion job started job=emergency-20260314. initial 0/12 shards. logging job id to thread.

incident-bot: JOB UPDATE emergency-20260314 3/12 shards complete. Mirrors returning 200s on GET.

customers-ops: sending short customer note to affected list: "We've observed third-party hosting rate limits causing delayed cold-starts. We're failing over to cached mirrors and expect improvements within 20-30 minutes. Apologies for disruption." :email:

eli-nguyen: runtime change: treat HF 429 as transient and enable `prefer_cached_variants` for dev/free namespaces. Deployed feature-flag hf429_fallback=true.

infra-sre: metrics: runtime error rate for generation requests dropped from ~6% -> ~1.5% after first mirror shards landed. Still seeing occasional failures for rare shards not yet mirrored.

oncall-pager: handoff to @maria-khan for extended watch. Handoff summary:
- Mitigations applied: emergency mirroring, prefetch throttling, fallback variants.
- Current status: partial mitigation; mirrors replacing many HF fetches; error rate decreased but not zero.
- Tasks: follow HF ticket HF-2026-331, finish mirror consistency sweep, consider dedicated egress IP pool for fetchers.
- Escalation contact: @eli-nguyen, @dmitri-ops

maria-khan: adding runbook note to thread: if HF 429s persist after promotion: reduce fetcher concurrency to 2, enable global prefer_cached, escalate mirror promotion priority to high, and consider temporary rate-limited rollout pauses. Keep hf429_fallback enabled until HF confirms OK.

incident-bot: PAGED @dmitri-ops for escalation review.

dmitri-ops: joining. initial suggestions: negotiate authenticated fetch tokens with HF for our dedicated egress IPs and add automated mirror prewarming for any model in a rollout. Will draft proposal.

hf-support-bot: HF reply: We detected elevated anonymous download rates from your org and applied short-lived throttling. Recommend using authenticated endpoints or mirrored artifacts for high-volume workloads. Support ticket HF-2026-331 created.

maria-khan: mirror sweep started to catch missing shards; ETA ~40m. I'll keep an eye on tail errors and mirror consistency.

customers-ops: updated customers: "We're routing model fetches to our mirrors and expect normalized cold-start behavior soon. We'll share a full incident summary when complete." :phone:

oncall-pager: closing the active paging loop for this shift. Incident remains open (SEV-2) until HF confirms throttle lifted and mirror sweep is done. Handoff note: continue monitoring 5xx rates and keep hf429_fallback flag on.

eli-nguyen: follow-ups created:
- infra-sre: implement authenticated fetch paths + token rotation (owner: infra-sre)
- runtime-team: auto-promote mirrors when prewarm detected (owner: runtime-team)
- bizops: negotiate HF higher-tier download allowances for critical customers (owner: bizops)

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE status=mitigated_partial last_update=2026-03-14T10:12:00Z. Archive when postmortem doc present.

maria-khan: key takeaway: canary + aggressive prefetch spike created a self-inflicted HF hammering event. We'll include prefetch-smoothing in rollout playbooks and add telemetry to detect prefetch storms.

eli-nguyen: thanks team. If HF confirms throttle removal and mirrors verify, we'll proceed to write a SEA style postmortem and schedule follow-ups.
